items.title: Colour Theory Has Politics - Paul Lessard
items.summary: Paul Lessard on why the representations we arrive at don't have to converge. Colour theory looks as if it simply is, but it carries politics and economics. His example is Faith Ringgold, the Black American painter and quilter, and the posters she made for the Black Panthers: backgrounds of orange and deep green, and shadows lighter than their surroundings, but purple, because she wanted to centre Black people rather than draw an abstract black line between background and foreground. We reach conclusions that work, he argues, but there was an enormous, likely infinite, range of others we could have reached.

items.title: AI Helped Beginners Far More Than Experts
items.summary: Imagine spending eight years getting great at your job, then watching a chatbot whisper all your secrets to the new guy. A study of 5,172 customer support agents found that an AI assistant helped them resolve about 15% more issues per hour on average, and about 30% more for newer and less-skilled workers, while the most experienced agents saw small gains. The researchers think the AI was spreading the methods of the best workers to everyone else. That’s good news if you’re new, but if you’re the expert, some of what set you apart may now be easier for others to pick up. The study didn’t look at pay, so the open question is what companies will still pay extra for. What do you think it is?

We dive into the rise of alternative clouds, the growing demand for AI inference, and the physical constraints that are forcing the entire infrastructure industry to rethink how it operates. Along the way, we explore the environmental impact of AI, the potential to reuse data center heat to power communities, and why a more diverse ecosystem of cloud providers could drive the next wave of innovation.

Zach also shares a bold prediction: Apple could become one of the world's largest AI inference providers within just a few years as on device AI changes where and how computation happens.

Finally, we examine what all of this means for engineering leaders — from choosing the right infrastructure to understanding the real-world impact of their technical decisions and building software that makes more responsible use of resources.
